subject: [Prop Digest] First-time buyer scheme: 'not supercharge', says Bellway
opener: Monday, and the Chancellor's new first-time buyer scheme is already getting a cold reception from the people who'd have to build the homes. Coffee up, let's go.

stories.text: The Chancellor has announced Your First Home, a scheme for first-time buyers. Bellway's Jason Honeyman told The Times it will "not supercharge" housebuilding, and The Negotiator's headline calls the boost "modest". **Why it matters:** if the builders themselves think it's a nudge rather than a shove, don't expect a sudden wave of new homes. Watch the detail, because the scheme only helps if it actually gets more sites moving.
stories.headline: Your First Home won't supercharge building, says Bellway

stories.text: A study by Let Compliance says mortgage interest takes £49.10 of every £100 of rent, income tax takes £9.94 and compulsory fees take £1.21. **Why it matters:** that's the sum landlords are weighing up when they decide whether to stay in the game, and it's a grim sum.
stories.headline: Landlords keep £39.75 of every £100 in rent

stories.text: Analysts warn that Rightmove's grip on estate agents is coming under growing scrutiny as the market weakens. **Why it matters:** portals can charge what they like while agents have no choice, but a weak market gives agents a reason to start asking awkward questions.
stories.headline: Rightmove's dominance faces a tougher test

stories.text: A long-established estate agency has completed the acquisition of a rival's lettings portfolio. The summary doesn't say much more than that. **Why it matters:** with lettings under pressure, buying someone else's landlords is a quicker route to growth than building your own from scratch.
stories.headline: Independent agency buys a rival's lettings portfolio

stories.text: Andrew Asaam of Lloyds says the "challenging economic backdrop" is having a big impact on the property market, against a backdrop of the steepest house price drop in three years. **Why it matters:** when a lender says the economy is the problem, that's a warning, not a shrug.
stories.headline: Lloyds says the economy is hitting house prices hard

stories.text: LRG's Neil Louth says upfront information gives buyers greater confidence in the offer they're making. **Why it matters:** if buyers feel surer of their offers, they're less likely to pull out later, which is the bit agents actually care about.
stories.headline: LRG says upfront information helps buyers commit

stories.text: Virelle's Emily Robison says landlords who kept their portfolios are seeing stronger tenant demand and potentially better yields. **Why it matters:** the sellers have left the building, so the ones who stayed are getting the rewards. Take that with a pinch of salt, since it's the view of someone who sells the service.
stories.headline: Virelle says landlords who held on are doing well

stories.text: The housing investment and management company HSPG is demerging, with its activities continuing through two independent businesses. Sevet will be led by Guy Horne and Highdale by David Searle. **Why it matters:** a founder-led split usually means each half has to prove it can stand alone.
stories.headline: HSPG splits in two as founders go their own way
